words.definition: The habitual accusation of logical fallacies, sometimes based on superficial resemblance rather than actual logical structure, coupled with a failure to recognize equivalent fallacies in one's own reasoning.
examples: I hate it when people on social media employ falluscism because they don't have any expertise in actual rhetoric.

words.definition: Worthy of note, as judged by the observer, especially as it happens.
A spontaneous, surreal moment caused by a small deviation from the status quo such that it reveals a dramatically different context in an otherwise familiar situation.
examples: Was at a LAN party the other day. Having to talk over voice chat whilst the other person is right next to me was such a surtext.

words.definition: A person who can only analyze superficially. Often evaluating on the most basic level whilst denouncing any deeper analysis.
words.notes: Often used in the context of media consumption.

words.definition: A person whose cultural identity constitutes only the most popular and immediately prevalent products of the prevailing zeitgeist, such that their cultural consumption exhibits little individual differentiation.
examples: Had a guy the other day come in with a puffer jacket, three stipes joggings, and nikes, whilst listening to the billboard top 40. That's a cultural antithesist if I ever saw one.
